_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the only thing that ever promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, behind its own pull request — see that file's own doc comment for why the human checkpoint lives there instead of here. Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved' (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). A human's actual review happens by reading/merging the review agent's PR, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: Hope Mill Theatre
suggestions.reason: A converted cotton mill on Pollard Street, opened by two directors chasing Off West End intimacy — Fringe Venue of the Year, and every seat close enough to see the actors breathe.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via hopemilltheatre.co.uk (official site) and Wikipedia — 113 Pollard Street, Ancoats/New Islington, Manchester M4 7JA, in the Grade II* listed Hope Mill building. Founded 2015 by Joseph Houston and William Whelton; won Fringe Venue of the Year at The Stage Awards 2018. Independent single-site theatre — no second venue found. Fills Ancoats' real Do-category gap (previously zero real Do venues in the district; one pending, Hallé St Peter's). Coordinates geocoded from the 113 Pollard Street M4 7JA address. PERFORMING ARTS type already exists (Royal Exchange Theatre). Confidence: high.

suggestions.name: Another Hand
suggestions.reason: Twenty-four covers up a flight of painted steps on Deansgate Mews, low-intervention plates built around whatever Cinderwood's growers sent over that morning.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the Michelin Guide UK listing, Manchester Confidential's review and thegreatnorthern.com (the building's own site) — Unit F, 253 Deansgate, Mews Level, Manchester M3 4EN. Independent 24-seat bistro opened 2022 by Julian Pizer and Max Yorke (also behind 3 Hands Deli, a takeaway/deli concept, not a second full restaurant of the same name) — single-site restaurant, no second 'Another Hand' found. Fills Deansgate's real Eat-category gap (previously zero real Eat venues; one pending, Podium Restaurant). Coordinates from the Great Northern Warehouse/Deansgate Mews geocoded position. SMALL PLATES type already exists (Erst, Victors). Confidence: high.

suggestions.name: King Street Townhouse Spa
suggestions.reason: A subterranean ESPA spa under a Grade II Italianate former bank on King Street, Himalayan salt cave included — the infinity pool upstairs is for residents, the day spa isn't.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via kingstreettownhouse.co.uk (official site), ESPA's own venue page and Good Spa Guide — 10 Booth Street, Manchester M2 4AW, inside the King Street Townhouse hotel (an 1872 former bank, Grade II listed). Single physical spa; the hotel is owned by THG (also owner of Hale Country Club & Spa, already pending in this queue) but this is one site, not a spa chain — same single-site-under-corporate-ownership test already applied there. King Street sits almost equidistant between this app's Deansgate and Spinningfields centroids; placed in Spinningfields as the closer of the two and the district this stretch is most commonly grouped with locally. Fills Spinningfields' real Do-category gap (previously zero real Do venues; one pending, Smolensky Gallery). Coordinates from the 10 Booth Street M2 4AW address. New type for this queue (SPA already used once, in the pending Hale Country Club & Spa entry) — maps to the 'Spa & wellness' onboarding tile. Confidence: medium-high (district boundary is a judgment call; the venue itself is well-verified).

suggestions.name: Evelyn's Cafe Bar
suggestions.reason: Brunch classics by day, then the charcoal Inka grill takes over after dark — Persian and Pan-Asian small plates in a room that never quite decides which meal it's for, on purpose.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via evelyns.co (official booking site), Manchester Confidential and Creative Tourist — G18 Smithfield Building, 4 Tib Street, Manchester M4 1NB. Owned by the Zanna Group, which also runs Mughli (Rusholme) and Queenswood (Manchester) — three distinct single-concept restaurants under one small local group, not multiple branches of 'Evelyn's' itself; the same type of grouping already accepted in this app's data (Craig's/Ivy Spinningfields, Church Inn/Bull's Head). Fills Northern Quarter's real Eat-category gap (previously zero real Eat venues; one pending, BAB NQ). Coordinates from the Smithfield Building/4 Tib Street M4 1NB address. SMALL PLATES type already exists (Erst, Victors, Another Hand above). Confidence: high.

suggestions.name: Clark Art
suggestions.reason: Bill Clark's own gallery on Ashley Road since 1999, deep in L.S. Lowry and the northern painters he's written the books on — a private dealer's eye, not a gallery chain's algorithm.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via artsy.net (Clark Art's own partner page), an Antiques Trade Gazette profile of owner Bill Clark, and halebarns.com's village directory — 155 Ashley Road, Hale Village, Altrincham WA14 2UW. Independent single-site gallery, established 1999, owned/run by Bill Clark, an acknowledged L.S. Lowry expert and author — no second Clark Art location found. Fills Hale's real Do-category gap (previously zero real Do venues; one pending, Hale Country Club & Spa). Coordinates anchored to Hale's own Ashley Road/village centre (close to docs/data/districts.json's own Hale centroid) since an independent street-level geocode for 155 Ashley Road wasn't returned — approximate but on the correct street, not a district centroid used for convenience. ART GALLERY type already exists (Manchester Art Gallery, Ricardo Van Parmar Gallery). Confidence: high on the venue being real/independent; medium on the exact coordinate.

suggestions.name: Waugh Brow Farm Shop
suggestions.reason: Dave and Ruth Jones's own cattle and pigs, twenty yards from the counter that sells them — a working farm since 1985, with a café tacked on for people who came for bacon and stayed for cake.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via waughbrowfarm.uk (official site), the Food Standards Agency hygiene ratings register and BigBarn's producer directory — Smith Lane, Mobberley, Knutsford WA16 6JZ. Genuine family-run working farm (Dave and Ruth Jones, 200 acres, own cattle/pigs/sheep) with an attached butcher and café, trading since 1985 — single site, no chain footprint. Fills Mobberley's real Eat-category gap (previously zero real Eat venues; one pending, Barnshaw Smithy, on the same lane between Mobberley and Ashley). New type, FARM SHOP, left category-only (Eat) like CANTONESE ROAST/GREEK TAVERNA/BRUNCH SPOT since no existing tile fits a working-farm shop-and-café precisely — needs mapping in src/lib/scoring/tile-catalog-map.ts's CATEGORY_BY_VENUE_TYPE if promoted. Coordinates from the WA16 6JY postcode centroid (Smith Lane) since the exact 6JZ address wasn't independently geocodable — street-level approximation, not a district centroid. Confidence: high on the venue; medium on the exact coordinate.

suggestions.name: Yang Sing
suggestions.reason: Three floors of a Grade II-listed Princess Street townhouse, family-run since the 1970s — bottomless yum cha that still draws a queue nobody seems to mind.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via visitmanchester.com, Hardens and Tripadvisor — 34 Princess Street, Manchester M1 4JY, a Grade II listed building. Family-run Cantonese institution operating since the late 1970s; has a sibling, Little Yang Sing, at 17 George Street — same family, same small footprint already accepted elsewhere in this app's data (Church Inn/Bull's Head, Craig's/Ivy Spinningfields) — only the flagship Yang Sing suggested here to avoid double-counting one family group. Adds a second real Eat venue to Chinatown (previously only Happy Seasons). New type, DIM SUM, left category-only (Eat) since no existing tile/type fits a dim sum specialist as precisely as CANTONESE ROAST fits Happy Seasons — needs mapping in tile-catalog-map.ts if promoted. Coordinates from the 34 Princess Street M1 4JY address. Confidence: high. Note: Chinatown's Drink category remains a genuine, unfilled gap — searched repeatedly this run but found no independent bar clearly both inside Chinatown's own footprint and clear of a chain/regional-pub-group flag; left for a future run rather than forcing a weak match.

suggestions.name: Flawd Wine
suggestions.reason: A waterside bottle shop on the New Islington marina that doubles as a bar — walk-ins only, a cheese board built to match whatever's open, and a wine list that skips anything you'd call conventional.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via flawdwine.co (official site), Manchester's Finest, Creative Tourist and wineanorak.com — Unit 3, Mansion House, Marina Promenade, New Islington, Manchester M4 6JL (an initial search surfaced a Deansgate address under 'Flawd', which turned out on closer checking to actually belong to Evuna's second site, not Flawd's — corrected to Flawd's own confirmed New Islington address before including it here). Independent natural wine bar and bottle shop opened 2021 by the same trio behind Higher Ground (Michelin-listed, city centre) and Cinderwood Market Garden (their own farm, which also supplies Erst and Another Hand, both already in this app's data) — Flawd itself is single-site, no second Flawd location found. New Islington sits within Ancoats' territory as this app already treats it (Ancoats' own seed notes reference canalside/mill-district character). Adds to Ancoats' Drink coverage (previously Jane Eyre, plus one pending, Nam) with a genuinely different, daytime-capable format. Coordinates from the Marina Promenade/New Islington geocoded position. WINE BAR type already exists (The Old Cellars, The Wine Cellar, ATOMECA Wine Bar pending). Confidence: high.

suggestions.name: Reserve at The Rex
suggestions.reason: Three separate terraces above a former bank on King Street, each with its own name and its own hour of the day it does best — arrive before the swing band starts if you want a seat outside.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via rexhotel.co.uk (official site) and Manchester's Finest — 100 King Street, Manchester M2 4WU, top floor of The Rex (rebranded 2026 from Hotel Gotham). Members'/hotel rooftop bar with three terraced 'wings'; the hotel is one of four individually-branded, distinctly-named boutique hotels under Leonardo's Limited Edition collection (The Rex, The Dilly London, The Grand Brighton, The Midland Manchester) — each a unique property, not a repeated chain brand, the same distinction already relied on for Refuge (Principal-owned) and Podium (Hilton-owned) in this app's existing data. King Street sits between Deansgate and Spinningfields' centroids; placed in Spinningfields alongside King Street Townhouse Spa (also in this batch) as the closer/commonly-grouped district for this stretch. Fills a real Spinningfields Drink gap (previously zero real Drink venues; one pending, ATOMECA Wine Bar). Coordinates from the 100 King Street M2 4WU address. ROOFTOP type already exists (20 Stories). Confidence: medium-high (venue and ownership well-verified; exact district placement is a judgment call given King Street's position between two districts).
